_about: Which IEC 62304 requirements apply to which software safety class, at sub-clause level. Kept separate from phases.json so this mapping can be reviewed on its own, and because it is regulatory fact rather than course content.
_source: IEC 62304:2006+AMD1:2015, Table A.1 (informative), cross-checked line by line against the [Class ...] tags in the normative text of Clauses 5 to 9. Where the two could differ the normative text governs, as the standard states Table A.1 is provided for convenience only.
_resolvedItems: 5.7.5 - CONFIRMED 30 July 2026. The normative text carries NO [Class ...] tag for this sub-clause; Amendment 1 replaced it in full and did not assign one. A/B/C is recorded on three grounds: Table A.1 assigns '5.7 All requirements' to all three classes; every other sub-clause of 5.7 (5.7.1 to 5.7.4) is explicitly tagged [Class A, B, C]; and software system testing applies to all classes, so a record-keeping requirement supporting it logically does too. Note this is the ONE entry in this file derived from the annex plus the absence of a restriction, rather than from a normative tag - worth knowing if anyone ever asks where it comes from.
_notes: Clause 4 carries no per-requirement [Class ...] tags; the standard's note says the tags appear in the clauses and subclauses that FOLLOW Clause 4. Table A.1 gives Clause 4 as all classes.

Amendment 1 changed applicability in several places that a reader working from a 2006 copy would get wrong: 5.7 (all requirements) moved from B,C to A,B,C; 6.2.3 moved from B,C to A,B,C, making Clause 6 uniformly all-classes; and 5.8.1, 5.8.2, 5.8.7 and 5.8.8 moved from B,C to A,B,C. 5.1.12 is new in Amendment 1 at B,C.
An empty classes array means the sub-clause was removed by Amendment 1 and carries no requirement.
